default_answers.alibi: I told you — I stepped out for some air before opening. It was a normal morning until Elias Grant screamed.
default_answers.timeline: Prepping the cafe, mostly. Chairs, coffee machine, the float. The same as every morning.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: They was here first thing. After that I was busy with the counter.
default_answers.relationship: They owned the cafe. I run it. We kept things professional.
default_answers.evidence: I don't know anything about that.
default_answers.location: I don't spend much time thinking about that place, to be honest.

default_answers.alibi: Doing my round, mate. Van by the square, crates in and out. Same as every day.
default_answers.timeline: On my round somewhere. It all blurs together a bit, honestly.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Properly spoke to them? Day before yesterday, when I dropped the coffee order.
default_answers.relationship: Nadia Cole was alright. Paid on time, tipped at Christmas. No trouble between us.
default_answers.evidence: Couldn't tell you anything about that.
default_answers.location: I'm all over the village in a morning, take your pick.

rules.answer_text: Right, so — I was down the alley end around then. Saw someone in a blue coat come in from the square about a quarter to... no, closer to ten-to. Went towards the cafe's back door. Didn't see the face but — that's Marcus Bell's coat, everyone knows it. And later there was this thud from inside. Dull, like a sack of flour going over. I didn't think anything of it. You don't, do you.

claims.summary: Priya Shah says she saw someone in a blue coat — she assumes Marcus Bell — enter the alley at about 06:52 and head for the cafe's rear door.
Priya Shah says she heard a dull thud from the cafe's back rooms while she was in the alley, around 07:01.

suggested_followups: Why were you in the alley at that time?

default_answers.alibi: I was at the clinic, then I came here for my meeting with Nadia Cole. You know the rest.
default_answers.timeline: Paperwork at the shop, then the clinic, then... the cafe.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Alive? At twenty past seven. I gave them a note about our meeting.
default_answers.relationship: We were business partners. They put money into my shop. It was... complicated lately.
default_answers.evidence: I can't help you with that.
default_answers.location: I know the village as well as anyone. What of it?

rules.answer_text: From about twenty to eight I was at the clinic — Ben Carter was taking my blood pressure, of all things. I'd been wound up about the meeting. I left just before eight, waited here at a table, and at ten past I went looking for him myself. I found him.

claims.summary: Elias Grant says he was at the clinic with Ben Carter from about 06:45 to 07:05, then waited in the cafe.

suggested_followups: Why were you so wound up?

rules.answer_text: So it's true. Isabella Reed. She promised me that expansion two years ago — I built my plans on it. If you're asking whether I was angry: yes. Angry enough to demand a meeting. Not angry enough for... whatever you're implying. I was with Ben Carter when it happened, ask him.

claims.summary: Elias Grant admits the partnership betrayal gave his a grievance, but points to his clinic alibi.

default_answers.alibi: In my yard. Working. Like every morning.
default_answers.timeline: Yard, mostly. Timber doesn't stack itself.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Outside the cafe, around seven. We had words. I'm not going to pretend we didn't.
default_answers.relationship: We did business. It went sour. That's between me and them.

rules.answer_text: From a quarter past seven I was in my yard. Timber delivery came — big one. Driver, Col Hartley, was with me signing sheets and unloading until gone eight. Check with them if you don't believe me. I've nothing to hide about where I was.

claims.summary: Clara Wells says she was in her yard with delivery driver Col Hartley from 06:20 until after 07:05.

suggested_followups: What were you and Nadia Cole arguing about at 06:10?

rules.answer_text: Eight thousand. There, I've said the number. They'd have ruined me by lunchtime and called it principle. But I was in my yard with Col when it happened, and thank God for that delivery, because I know how this looks.

default_answers.alibi: I was in the bookshop stockroom, sorting the delivery. I didn't see anything.
default_answers.timeline: The stockroom, mostly. It was a big delivery.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Yesterday afternoon. They came by the shop.
default_answers.relationship: They was kind to me. Kinder than people knew. I can't believe this has happened.
default_answers.location: I mostly go between home and the shop.

rules.answer_text: ...Alright. Please don't take this the wrong way. I was in the alley, for a few minutes, around a quarter to eight. With Priya Shah. We've been seeing each other — Elias Grant doesn't approve of that kind of thing at the shop, so we keep it quiet. We stood by the back door and talked, that's all. We heard a sort of thud from the cafe side and then a door, and we got nervous someone would see us, so we left. Priya Shah went to her van. I went inside. That's everything, I promise.

claims.summary: Isabella Reed admits she and Priya Shah were secretly meeting in the alley from about 06:50 to just before 07:05, and heard a thud and a door from the cafe side.

suggested_followups: What exactly did you hear from the cafe?
Did you see who came out of the rear door?

default_answers.alibi: I was at the clinic from ten to seven. I had a patient with me over that window, as it happens.
default_answers.timeline: Clinic, mostly. I crossed the square a couple of times.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Through the cafe window this morning, about twenty to eight.
default_answers.relationship: A neighbour. Decent man under the gruffness. They sponsored half this village one way or another.
default_answers.evidence: I only know what I saw and heard, and I'll keep to that.
default_answers.location: Ask me something specific and I'll tell you what I saw.

rules.answer_text: Clinic, from ten to seven onwards. And before you ask — Elias Grant was with me from about twenty to eight until eight. Blood pressure check. He was strung tight over some meeting, but he was in my chair the whole time.

claims.summary: Ben Carter confirms Elias Grant was at the clinic with him from about 06:45 to 07:05.

rules.answer_text: I crossed the square about twenty to eight, past the cafe window. Nadia Cole was talking to someone — low, but the window was cracked open. I caught '...storage room, before we open...'. Couldn't see or hear who she was talking to. It only means something now, doesn't it.

claims.summary: Ben Carter heard Nadia Cole say 'storage room, before we open' to someone at about 06:45.

suggested_followups: Who was in the cafe at 06:45?

default_answers.alibi: My bench, six-forty until the scream. Best seat in the village.
default_answers.timeline: On the bench. I see everything from there — well. Nearly everything, it turns out.
default_answers.last_seen_victim: Going into their cafe this morning, quarter to seven, same as forty years of mornings.
default_answers.relationship: Nadia Cole? Knew her since she was a boy. Stubborn as a gatepost.
default_answers.location: From my bench you can see the cafe, the fountain, the bookshop and the clinic door. Ask away.

rules.answer_text: Forty years I knew them. And I'll tell you something for nothing: last week, in the cafe, I heard them say to somebody — quiet, but furious, the way they got — 'You have until tomorrow.' Never saw who. Kitchen doorway, my back was to it. But Nadia Cole didn't threaten people for sport. Somebody in this village was living on borrowed time, and I'd say the loan came due.

claims.summary: Owen Price heard Nadia Cole tell someone 'You have until tomorrow' in the cafe last week, but didn't see who.

suggested_followups: Could it have been a member of staff they was talking to?
How did you two first meet?

rules.answer_text: Marcus Bell went out the front just before the quarter hour and turned towards the square. Now here's the thing — he says fountain, I hear. I face that fountain, young detective. My eyes aren't what they were, and I did have my crossword. But I don't recall seeing his at it. Clara Wells, though — you should have heard her this morning. That's your man, I'd stake my pension.

claims.summary: Owen Price, who faces the fountain from his bench, does not recall seeing Marcus Bell at the fountain between 06:50 and 07:05 — though he admits his attention was on his crossword.
Owen Price insists Clara Wells must be the killer because of the morning argument.

suggested_followups: How sure are you that Marcus Bell wasn't at the fountain?
